nodes.action: deployed without running the test suite
the regression reached every user and forced a full rollback
set up a CI gate that blocks merges without tests
released via canary deployment to 5 percent of traffic first
skipped the flaky tests to make CI green
ran the full regression suite before release
switched to mandatory peer review plus CI, since tests alone missed edge cases

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Morning, Marcus. You look like you've been here since dawn.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Ha, close. I was reviewing the deploy logs from last night. Did you push that auth refactor without running the test suite?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah... I was in a hurry, and the suite takes forever. I figured it was a small change.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Small change, big consequences. A regression slipped into production — the session timeout logic is broken. Users are getting logged out mid-checkout.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Oh no. How far did it spread?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Every user. We had to do a full rollback at 3 AM. That's the second time this month.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I'm sorry. I'll set up a CI gate that blocks merges without tests. That should stop this from happening again.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good. Let's do that today. I don't want to be paged again.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey, I saw the CI gate is live. Nice work.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Thanks. It's been smooth — untested code never reached production since we turned it on.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: I noticed you also did a canary deployment for the new payment endpoint. Only 5 percent of traffic first?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah, that felt safer. But I had to skip the flaky tests to make CI green — the ones that randomly fail on timing. I marked them as skipped.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hmm, that's a bit risky. But I guess the gate still passed.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: It did. And the canary caught nothing, so we rolled out fully. But honestly, I'm a little worried.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Worried about what?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: That we're relying too much on the gate. Let's see how the next release goes.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Joanna, we need to talk. The last release — the one with the skipped flaky tests — a regression slipped into production again.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: What? The CI gate was green. How did that happen?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: The tests passed, but they didn't cover the edge case with null user IDs. It hit all users before we caught it. We rolled back again.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Damn. So the CI gate... it turns out that wasn't enough. I was wrong about that being the fix.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Yeah. Tests alone missed it. We need something more.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I've been thinking. We replaced the CI-only approach with mandatory peer review plus CI. Every merge needs a human reviewer who actually understands the change, not just a green checkmark.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's a solid move. Peer review would have caught the null case — someone would have asked 'what if user is null?'

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Exactly. And I ran the full regression suite before this release — no skips. Regressions were caught before shipping this time.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good. Let's make sure the new process sticks. I'd rather have a slower pipeline than another 3 AM rollback.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Agreed. I'm done cutting corners.
